scope: Current single-vCPU retained-EPT direct handoff. Host means the L1 Linux kernel A or B running the microVM; physical L0 nested-KVM resources are outside the patch scope.
method: Rechecked current allocation/rebinding code and read the still-running generation-1000 soak VM without pausing or modifying its execution state. Re-read pointer fields at allocation-log offsets; did not decode opaque VMCS bytes.
interpretation: Object storage, pointer target storage, and the kernel/CPU identity represented by a value are separate properties.

Outside the shared kernel arena is a range classification, not proof that an arbitrary address is outside every possible CXL mapping. Source allocation paths identify the native resources listed here.
Native identity does not mean the bytes must physically be in DRAM: placing them on CXL NUMA RAM would not make scheduler, mm, FD, SRCU or per-CPU state usable by a different kernel.
Live pointers can change while a VM executes. This read-only review checked stable ownership/generation, not an atomic snapshot of the entire VM.
The initial IRQFD allocation-log fields refer to retired objects after the first detach. They are retained as historical evidence and excluded from current active-pointer claims.
Inactive optional allocation paths are distinguished from resources actually required by this configuration.

objects.data: 128MiB advertised guest RAM, including guest page tables and guest kernel objects
objects.storage: shared DAX [2MiB,130MiB)
objects.external_dependency: Host VMA/PTEs map these bytes; EPT maps the same physical backing
objects.handoff: Retain bytes and guest address space; destination maps the same HVA/PFNs

objects.data: struct kvm_vmx/struct kvm and struct vcpu_vmx/struct kvm_vcpu; embedded memslot roots, locks, notifier and SRCU wrappers
objects.storage: shared kernel DAX arena [256MiB,384MiB)
objects.external_dependency: Mixed: pool-internal pointers plus native mm/PID/per-CPU/code references
objects.handoff: Retain the object graph; replace only destination-native bindings. An embedded wrapper being shared does not imply its targets are shared.

objects.data: Guest register/control state backing, FPU/XSAVE image, CPUID/MCE arrays and emulator context
objects.storage: shared vCPU or separate DAX allocations
objects.external_dependency: Latest live state can reside in CPU registers or VMCS caches; emulator callbacks are kernel code
objects.handoff: Normal KVM exit/put and VMCS release complete the quiescent handoff boundary. Function references require matching code addresses.

objects.data: Kernel/userspace run page, PIO data page and configured coalesced-MMIO ring
objects.storage: DAX pages
objects.external_dependency: vCPU FD, VMA/PTEs and userspace mappings are native to each process/kernel
objects.handoff: Keep the backing pages; destination gets/reuses its own FD and mapping. kvm_run is an execution/exit interface, not the whole CPU state.

objects.data: kvm_memslots, kvm_memory_slot, GFN/HVA indexes and current architecture-specific slot arrays
objects.storage: shared VM storage and DAX allocations
objects.external_dependency: userspace_addr denotes an address in the owner's native mm
objects.handoff: Preserve slot contents under the fixed-HVA contract; check first/last destination PFN before installing native observers

objects.data: EPT root/leaves and kvm_mmu_page headers/registry
objects.storage: shared DAX; live root arena offset 0x73000
objects.external_dependency: Native struct page.private, slab/cache anchors, RCU machinery and CPU TLB
objects.handoff: Retain EPT pages with identical PFNs; bind local page.private for new headers and request TLB flush. Local slab anchors are reselected.

objects.data: MicroVM VMCS region allocated by the patched L1 KVM
objects.storage: one PAGE_SIZE-aligned DAX allocation; live arena offset 0x1d000, L1 physical address 0x3a001d000
objects.external_dependency: CPU VMCS ownership/cache and host-state field semantics
objects.handoff: Source loaded_vmcs_clear; destination loads the same region and prepares native host state/VPID. Opaque VMCS bytes are not interpreted as a portable C structure.

objects.data: vmcs01/loaded_vmcs, host-state cache, MSR bitmap and embedded MSR autoload arrays
objects.storage: loaded_vmcs and autoload arrays inside shared vcpu_vmx; MSR bitmap in a separate DAX page
objects.external_dependency: cpu/VPID values and list links refer to native CPU/per-CPU namespaces; host values in shared buffers still describe the current host
objects.handoff: Clear source CPU membership, allocate destination VPID, invalidate host-state caches and let destination load/entry paths prepare host values

objects.data: HOST_CR3, HOST_RSP, HOST_RIP, host GDT/IDT/TSS and FS/GS references
objects.storage: Field storage is in the DAX VMCS; cache storage is in the DAX loaded_vmcs
objects.external_dependency: Targets are the destination host's page tables, kernel stack, code and per-CPU descriptors
objects.reason: VM-exit must return into the currently executing kernel/task; sharing the numeric value cannot substitute for preparing that kernel's return context
objects.handoff: vmx_set_constant_host_state plus normal vCPU load and VM-entry host-state refresh; HOST_RSP is refreshed in the entry assembly path

objects.data: mm_struct, VMA tree, host HVA-to-PFN page tables and MMU notifier registry
objects.storage: native host kernel allocations; pointers/notifier wrapper inside shared kvm
objects.reason: They describe the current process address space and are registered with its kernel memory manager. Identical HVA numbers do not make the two mm objects identical.
objects.handoff: Unregister/drain source notifier and mmdrop source mm; mmgrab current->mm and register destination notifier

objects.data: task_struct, PID, native kernel/user stack, scheduler runqueue, thread/TLS and preemption machinery
objects.storage: native host runtime; vCPU pid/cpu/preempt-notifier fields are shared
objects.reason: Execution belongs to a task managed by one kernel's scheduler. Native saved stack/current-task state cannot be inherited by another kernel through a pointer copy.
objects.handoff: Drain source PID readers, clear old PID/cpu and initialize destination preempt notifier; destination executor thread enters KVM_RUN

objects.data: SRCU per-CPU reader/update allocations, kernel RCU queues and conditional xarray radix nodes
objects.storage: native allocations; SRCU/xarray wrappers and embedded RCU heads can be shared
objects.reason: Reader counts, callbacks and reclamation are coordinated by a particular kernel. Generic allocation paths have not been turned into a shared distributed runtime.
objects.handoff: Retain required reader drains; cleanup and reinitialize destination SRCU/index. Never-reused retired allocations permit selected callback-completion waits to remain off the critical path.
objects.qualification: A single index-0 xarray entry can be stored directly in the shared root; dynamic radix nodes are conditional, not an assertion that this run always allocated them.

objects.data: FD table, struct file/anon inode, eventfd_ctx, epoll registration and native socket/file state
objects.storage: native host kernel. kvm_kernel_irqfd wrapper is DAX-allocated; Rust FD wrappers can be in the DAX heap.
objects.reason: FD numbers and wait queues identify resources in a particular process/kernel. Moving wrapper bytes does not transfer those resources.
objects.handoff: Get/reuse destination VM/vCPU FD wrappers. Remove source IRQFD native observers and re-register A IRQFDs on return. Full ioeventfd/block/network/vsock handoff is not implemented.

objects.data: PIC/IOAPIC/LAPIC/PIT registers, pending state, clock/TSC values, timer/work wrappers and remaining-time anchors
objects.storage: shared DAX logical state and wrappers; native timer bases/queues, clock sources and PIT worker task
objects.reason: The host kernel dispatches timer interrupts/work on its CPUs and time domain. A source timer-base pointer is not a destination timer registration.
objects.handoff: Cancel/drain source work, retain logical state, reconnect a destination-local cached PIT worker, reinitialize hrtimers and rebase clock/TSC

objects.data: Kernel/module code, callback/ops tables, global VM list, PM registration, per-CPU current VMCS/list, VPID bitmap and VMXON regions
objects.storage: host code/global/per-CPU storage; pointers and list nodes can be embedded in DAX objects
objects.reason: These service all VMs/tasks of a kernel/CPU and are not private portable microVM state. Code is already installed on both nodes.
objects.handoff: Re-register native lists/notifiers and CPU bindings. Some callbacks are explicitly reinitialized; other raw callbacks remain valid only under the identical code-address contract.
objects.qualification: VMXON areas are allocated at module initialization before this lab enables the DAX pool. They differ from the later per-microVM VMCS allocation.

objects.data: Debugfs dentry/VFS registry and optional statistics presentation
objects.storage: Initially native dentry with some DAX statistics payloads; current live debugfs_dentry is ERR_PTR(-ENOENT)
objects.reason: Optional host diagnostics rather than guest execution state; no requirement to carry them with the VM
objects.handoff: Destroy source debugfs and clear its fields; current attach does not recreate debugfs

objects.data: struct page/dev_pagemap identity, page.private, slab descriptors, local gen_pool/control anchors
objects.storage: kernel-local metadata; EPT/page bytes, shared bump/header and Rust free-list are DAX
objects.reason: Each kernel maintains its own page/allocator namespace and lifetimes. This is separate from the physical data page being shared.
objects.handoff: Rebind local EPT page.private and slab anchors. Shared bump allocation is preserved and not reclaimed until lab shutdown; local gen_pool available count does not describe shared bump usage.

objects.data: VM mutex/spinlock/refcount storage versus task owners, native waiters and futex queues
objects.storage: Lock/refcount bytes can be in DAX; contention identities/queues belong to native kernels
objects.reason: A kernel cannot wake or schedule a foreign kernel's task by interpreting a shared waiter pointer
objects.handoff: Use cooperative quiescent single-owner handoff with no foreign lock waiters. Do not transfer a contended lock or blindly reset all locks/refcounts.

objects.data: Vmm/VmCommon, Box<Vcpu>, Rust containers and device wrappers versus ELF text, stacks, TLS, early System allocations and native FDs
objects.storage: Post-activation global Rust heap allocations in DAX [512MiB,576MiB); native process mappings remain local
objects.reason: Replacing GlobalAlloc does not relocate the whole process or every mmap/libc/kernel allocation. Rust vtables and FD values still describe A's runtime.
objects.handoff: Firecracker remains on A; B uses the existing native executor. A new process does not attach to and resume the old Rust heap.

objects.data: APIC-access/real-mode TSS/identity-map helper pages, APICv/IPIv/PML, APF, steal time, PMU, NX recovery and nested guest-hypervisor resources
objects.storage: Conditional unmodified helper mappings may use native anonymous RAM; other feature objects vary by allocation path
objects.current_status: Live unrestricted_guest=Y, enable_apicv=N, flexpriority=N; current boot disables PML/preemption timer. TSS/identity/APIC-access helper paths are not active in the supported configuration. APF/steal/PMU are excluded and a live NX recovery worker is rejected.
objects.reason: These are unsupported/conditional paths, not proof that the current 128MiB RAM contains native anonymous pages
objects.handoff: Do not extend current claims to those features. Supporting them requires separate placement and native-binding work.

objects.data: Live CPU registers, internal VMCS/TLB caches, plus physical L0 KVM's VMCS02/nested-EPT/runtime
objects.storage: CPU hardware and unmodified L0 host resources, outside the shared-object placement work
objects.reason: Running state must be quiesced before another owner uses the shared backing. Nested virtualization adds an outer execution layer beyond the patched L1 kernel.
objects.handoff: The DAX VMCS claim is about the region allocated by patched L1 KVM. Bare-metal multi-host VMCS compatibility/coherence and relocation of L0 resources are not validated.

necessity_review.scope: Fresh source purpose/reference audit; native identity vs physical storage; reverse references/tagged IDs; conditional MSR/PMU-filter gaps. No new runtime changes or VM execution tests.
